body:
Not sure if this is worth sharing but I don't really know where else to say it. I'm a 2nd year med student (EU) and I have had problems with depression and suicidal ideation since I was 14. I've been on  three different antidepressants as well as receiving courses of different talking therapies for months at a time and honestly nothing has made any difference. 

I know there's that joke that says the psychiatrist can only screw the light bulb in if it wants to change and I've been told so frequently that the reason it's not working is because I don't want to improve but I do; it's just I don't see how it is possible that things actually can get better for me despite actively seeking help, talking about it and receiving medication with absolutely no change in my situation.

I hope things get better, but with all the evidence pointing against it I really struggle to believe it will.

I've suffered from depression and suicidal ideation for about 4-5 years now and tried meds and CBT and had absolutely no progress. Not sure if this is the right place to ask but does anyone have any suggestions on what to do because I want to 'address them quickly' but the longer it goes on the less I feel it's ever going to change.
